virals.text:
its live 

everyone now has an open source AI video editor

you just give this skill file to your coding agent and it can now editing videos at a top 1% level

how does it work

- word by word transcription that can do 1 hour of source video in 2 minutes

- speaker diarization so it knows who's talking

- all the editing happens by claude code or grok bot or codex and can add motion graphics etc

- a 1 hour video gets rendered in minutes in the cloud and uploaded to this UI

- this is multiplayer, your team can then mark up the video with comments of feedback

- your coding agent can see that feedback and do the edits

- you can highlight word sections and delete them etc

- you can add features to this by just telling claude code "add this feature"

for a new render after this feedback, re render in minutes

everything it does

- upload every camera angle, the screen recording and each mic as its own file

- it syncs them by matching the audio

- every file gets transcribed on upload, each word tagged with who said it

- tell the agent "make a first cut, 30 seconds, vertical" and it reads the transcripts, picks the takes, cuts the ums and the dead air

- it switches to whoever is talking and cuts to the screen share when they talk about the screen

- crop and zoom on any clip

- comment on a frame or a time range, draw on the video, reply, resolve

- start a comment with @ agent and it becomes a task in the agent's queue

- the agent claims it, makes the edit, renders v2, replies with what it changed and the timecodes

- delete words in the script and playback skips them, cmd z brings them back

- share link so a client can watch and comment with no login

- every version is saved, v1 v2 v3

- export all the notes as markdown or csv

what it's built with

- whisperx for the word level transcript + speaker labels

- ffmpeg for every cut

- modal for the render. the edit gets split into 30 second chunks and they all render at the same time on 4 machines with 64 cores each

- a 48 minute podcast with 5.8 GB of source files rendered in 3 minutes 33 seconds

- chunks are cached so v2 only renders the 30 seconds you changed

- tesseract for the motion graphics

- hls for playback so a 1 hour video starts right away

- postgres for the comments, cuts and versions

- an mcp server with 22 tools so claude code, codex or cursor can drive the whole thing

- node, no framework, about 4,000 lines

- all of it runs on graphed cloud

the edit is just a json file. clips, cameras, mics

the agent writes the json and the cloud turns it into video

and then just give your agent this skill -

10 OPEN-SOURCE GITHUB REPOS TO MAKE YOUR AI APPS MORE SECURE AND TRUSTWORTHY 🔐

Building an AI app is exciting. But making sure it behaves safely, protects user data, and gives reliable answers is a whole different challenge.

These 10 open-source projects can help you build more secure and dependable AI applications:

1. Garak
Scan LLMs for security vulnerabilities and potential weaknesses.
https://t.co/nQ4LONyYdq

2. LLM Guard
Protect LLM applications from prompt injection, data leaks, and unsafe inputs.
https://t.co/FhydunYXEU

3. Guardrails AI
Validate model outputs and enforce structured responses.
https://t.co/2nEbOfmhVJ

4. Oxylabs Web API MCP
Connect AI agents to web data through an MCP server for research and data extraction.
https://t.co/UDqHKRZxM6

5. PromptBench
Benchmark LLMs across prompting techniques and adversarial attacks.
https://t.co/D5objIiCvP

6. Giskard
Test LLM applications for quality, reliability, and security issues.
https://t.co/IQndGXOhNt

7. LLM Attacks
Explore and reproduce published adversarial attacks on language models.
https://t.co/Rz68fZeOPx

8. Outlines
Generate structured and constrained outputs from language models.
https://t.co/7HkXlZhJOB

9. Instructor
Get validated, structured data from LLM responses using Python and Pydantic.
https://t.co/Qm5ZAesKlp

10. Haystack
Build LLM applications with modular pipelines and retrieval tools.
https://t.co/tiKh8oru6H

Why explore these repos?

They cover important parts of building trustworthy AI:

→ Security testing
→ Prompt injection protection
→ Output validation
→ Adversarial testing
→ Reliable structured responses
→ Better LLM application pipelines

AI apps shouldn't just be powerful. They should be safe, reliable, and predictable too.

🔖 Bookmark this list for your next AI project.

outsiders.text:
its live 

everyone now has an open source AI video editor

you just give this skill file to your coding agent and it can now editing videos at a top 1% level

how does it work

- word by word transcription that can do 1 hour of source video in 2 minutes

- speaker diarization so it knows who's talking

- all the editing happens by claude code or grok bot or codex and can add motion graphics etc

- a 1 hour video gets rendered in minutes in the cloud and uploaded to this UI

- this is multiplayer, your team can then mark up the video with comments of feedback

- your coding agent can see that feedback and do the edits

- you can highlight word sections and delete them etc

- you can add features to this by just telling claude code "add this feature"

for a new render after this feedback, re render in minutes

everything it does

- upload every camera angle, the screen recording and each mic as its own file

- it syncs them by matching the audio

- every file gets transcribed on upload, each word tagged with who said it

- tell the agent "make a first cut, 30 seconds, vertical" and it reads the transcripts, picks the takes, cuts the ums and the dead air

- it switches to whoever is talking and cuts to the screen share when they talk about the screen

- crop and zoom on any clip

- comment on a frame or a time range, draw on the video, reply, resolve

- start a comment with @ agent and it becomes a task in the agent's queue

- the agent claims it, makes the edit, renders v2, replies with what it changed and the timecodes

- delete words in the script and playback skips them, cmd z brings them back

- share link so a client can watch and comment with no login

- every version is saved, v1 v2 v3

- export all the notes as markdown or csv

what it's built with

- whisperx for the word level transcript + speaker labels

- ffmpeg for every cut

- modal for the render. the edit gets split into 30 second chunks and they all render at the same time on 4 machines with 64 cores each

- a 48 minute podcast with 5.8 GB of source files rendered in 3 minutes 33 seconds

- chunks are cached so v2 only renders the 30 seconds you changed

- tesseract for the motion graphics

- hls for playback so a 1 hour video starts right away

- postgres for the comments, cuts and versions

- an mcp server with 22 tools so claude code, codex or cursor can drive the whole thing

- node, no framework, about 4,000 lines

- all of it runs on graphed cloud

the edit is just a json file. clips, cameras, mics

the agent writes the json and the cloud turns it into video

get started free here - https://t.co/wZuSwrUfwn

and then just give your agent this skill -

10 OPEN-SOURCE GITHUB REPOS TO MAKE YOUR AI APPS MORE SECURE AND TRUSTWORTHY 🔐

Building an AI app is exciting. But making sure it behaves safely, protects user data, and gives reliable answers is a whole different challenge.

These 10 open-source projects can help you build more secure and dependable AI applications:

1. Garak
Scan LLMs for security vulnerabilities and potential weaknesses.
https://t.co/nQ4LONyYdq

2. LLM Guard
Protect LLM applications from prompt injection, data leaks, and unsafe inputs.
https://t.co/FhydunYXEU

3. Guardrails AI
Validate model outputs and enforce structured responses.
https://t.co/2nEbOfmhVJ

4. Oxylabs Web API MCP
Connect AI agents to web data through an MCP server for research and data extraction.
https://t.co/UDqHKRZxM6

5. PromptBench
Benchmark LLMs across prompting techniques and adversarial attacks.
https://t.co/D5objIiCvP

6. Giskard
Test LLM applications for quality, reliability, and security issues.
https://t.co/IQndGXOhNt

7. LLM Attacks
Explore and reproduce published adversarial attacks on language models.
https://t.co/Rz68fZeOPx

8. Outlines
Generate structured and constrained outputs from language models.
https://t.co/7HkXlZhJOB

9. Instructor
Get validated, structured data from LLM responses using Python and Pydantic.
https://t.co/Qm5ZAesKlp

10. Haystack
Build LLM applications with modular pipelines and retrieval tools.
https://t.co/tiKh8oru6H

Why explore these repos?

They cover important parts of building trustworthy AI:

→ Security testing
→ Prompt injection protection
→ Output validation
→ Adversarial testing
→ Reliable structured responses
→ Better LLM application pipelines

AI apps shouldn't just be powerful. They should be safe, reliable, and predictable too.

3. GitHub Copilot turns the recording into a list of steps you can edit.
4. One click turns it into a skill your agent can run, or an automation on a schedule.

It generalizes from one example, so recording yourself submitting one form teaches the agent to submit all of them.

Runs on Mac, Windows 11 and Ubuntu. Needs a GitHub account with Copilot access.
